## For elevation

Packages used: sf, ggplot2, classInt, dplyr.

```{r, message=FALSE}
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)
library(classInt)
library(dplyr)
```

Reading GeoJSON:
```{r}
DAs <- st_read('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/michellechuqi/geos472-group-map/main/webMapData.geojson')
```

Examining elevation distribution.
Note that elevation unit is metres above mean sea level.
```{r}
summary(DAs$elevation)
```

Elevation distribution visualised via histogram:
```{r}
ggplot(DAs, aes(x = elevation)) +
  geom_histogram(
    bins = 30,
    fill = "steelblue",
    colour = "black"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of DA Elevations",
    x = "Elevation (metres above mean sea level)",
    y = "Number of Dissemination Areas"
  )
```

Are DAs with no elevation data categorised as NA or 255?
```{r}
sum(is.na(DAs$elevation))
sum(DAs$elevation == 255)
```
There are 50 DAs with an elevation value of 255, aka with no elevation value available.
The DA with the highest actual elevation value is 247.

Calculating natural breaks ranges for 5 classes:
```{r}
nb_elevation <- classIntervals(DAs$elevation, n = 5, style = 'jenks')
nb_elevation$brks
```
So elevation should be classed as:

* 0 to 30, 
* 31 to 69, 
* 70 to 112, 
* 123 to 187, 
* 188 to 247.
A special class is for DAs with elevation = 255.


## For population
Summary statistics:
```{r}
summary(DAs$population)
```

Distribution of population via histogram:
```{r}
ggplot(DAs, aes(x = population)) +
  geom_histogram(
    bins = 30,
    fill = "steelblue",
    colour = "black"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of DA Populations",
    x = "Count population",
    y = "Number of Dissemination Areas"
  )
```

Summary statistics for population DENSITY:
```{r}
summary(DAs$pop_density)
```

Calculating natural breaks ranges for 5 classes:
```{r}
nb_pd <- classIntervals(DAs$pop_density, n = 5, style = 'jenks')
nb_pd$brks
```
Population density choropleth should be classed as:

* 0 to 4318, 
* 4319 to 10816, 
* 10817 to 22860,
* 22861 to 43398,
* 43399 to 76693.
